PullRequest.Title: sessions: report chat background changes in telemetry
PullRequest.Body:

Adds a `vscodeAgents.chatBackground/changed` telemetry event that is sent every time the Agents window chat background changes, however it was changed. Until now, background changes were not reported at all, except as part of the agent's generic tool telemetry, so we cannot measure how the appearance tools and the background picker are used.

## Event

| Field | Values |
|---|---|
| `source` | `agent` (Set Chat Background tool), `backgroundPicker` (Set Background...), `layoutPicker` (Change Background Layout...), `settings` (anything else: Settings editor, settings.json, Settings Sync, profile switch) |
| `background` | `userImage` (an image file from the user or an agent), `builtin` (the Codicons pattern), `none` (removed) |
| `change` | `background`, or `layout` when only the image layout changed |
| `layout` | the image layout, when the background is an image |
| `colorScheme` | `dark` or `light` (backgrounds are set separately for dark and light themes) |

All fields are bounded strings; image paths are never sent.

## Implementation

- `SessionsChatBackgroundService` reports the event from its configuration listener, so changes made outside the service (for example in settings.json) are included.
- `setBackground`, `clearBackground` and `setBackgroundImageLayout` now require a source. The service remembers it while writing the setting and attributes the resulting configuration change to it. The configuration service fires the change before the write resolves; any change that no caller claimed is reported as `settings`.
- The background and layout pickers pass their source, and the Set Chat Background tool passes `agent`.
- Only changes of what is shown are reported. The service compares the resolved background and image layout of each color scheme with the last reported ones, because a setting can change without changing the background: for example when the layout that is used by default is selected, the current image is selected again, or a path replaces a `file` URI of the same image.

## Notes for reviewers

- When an agent sets an image and a layout together, two events are sent: `background`, then `layout`. Count `change = background` for background changes.
- Layout previews in the picker are not reported, and neither is selecting the background, preset, or layout that is already shown, or removing a background when none is shown.
- Backgrounds made from the picker's Generate Background entry are applied by an agent, so they are reported as `agent`.
- This change has not landed on `main` yet; it targets `release/1.144` directly.

## How to test

Validation run on this branch:

- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot src/vs/sessions/services/chatBackground/test/browser/chatBackgroundService.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatBackgroundTool.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatBackgroundTint.test.ts`: passed (62 passing), including the new `reports each background change with its source` test, which also checks that selecting what is already shown is not reported.
- `npx tsc --project ./src/tsconfig.json --noEmit --skipLibCheck` (the `typecheck-client` command): passed, 0 errors.
- `npm run eslint -- <changed files>`: passed.
- `@vscode/telemetry-extractor` on `src/vs/sessions/services/chatBackground/browser`: passed. It resolves the event with owner `benibenj` and all five fields as `SystemMetaData` / `FeatureInsight`, none of them measurements.

Not run: manual testing in a running Agents window.

To try it manually, enable telemetry logging (Developer: Show Telemetry) in the Agents window, then change the background through the Set Background picker, the layout picker, an agent (with `chat.agentSessions.appearanceTools.enabled`), and settings.json, and check the `vscodeAgents.chatBackground/changed` events.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agents window creates and uses the chat-background service
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When the delayed service is first requested by the Sessions part or background-related contribution, construction now reads the configured background and layout for exactly two color schemes before the service is available.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed cardinality of two color schemes; no dependence on chat count, history, image size, or workspace size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous fixed-size initialization; no queue, parallel work, or contention is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The two resolved states are retained in a two-entry map and updated only when their settings change. There are no cold/warm misses or unbounded keys.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor and configuration access paths were inspected directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact configuration-read cost varies by host, but reads are in-memory getValue calls and the cardinality is fixed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds four bounded in-memory setting reads and two small retained records at first service use.

Scenarios.Scenario: User changes a background or commits a layout from the quick pick
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing user configuration update remains the awaited critical path. Its synchronous change event now compares the affected scheme's resolved background/layout and, only for a visible change, calls publicLog2. The telemetry path performs bounded cleaning/mixing and dispatches to appenders; desktop IPC dispatch is fire-and-forget rather than awaited by the picker.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the selected background or layout through IConfigurationService.updateValue to user configuration storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One write per committed picker choice; layout focus previews use persist=false and perform no write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same configuration updateValue call was directly awaited before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the picker action completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch the bounded chatBackground/changed telemetry payload to the telemetry appender channel on desktop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one IPC call for the affected scheme per actual displayed-state change; no IPC for focus previews or unchanged values.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No chat-background telemetry IPC was emitted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The channel call is initiated synchronously but its promise is not awaited, so transport completion is off the action's critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected background produces at most one event. A committed layout produces at most one event. The listener checks exactly two schemes; repeated selection of the same resolved state produces none.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Configuration updates retain their prior behavior. The new telemetry IPC is dispatched asynchronously without awaiting it; there is no per-item loop or burst beyond one event for the changed scheme.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The previous resolved state is kept per dark/light scheme, suppressing unchanged selections. No negative-cache distinction is needed because absence is represented explicitly and updated on relevant events.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: picker handlers, listener filtering, state comparison, telemetry service, and IPC appender implementations were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Appender implementation and transport latency vary by platform, but event frequency is user-driven and state-deduplicated.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new boundary is bounded, deduplicated, low-frequency, and not awaited; layout previews explicitly avoid telemetry and persistence.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent tool applies an image, preset, removal, or image layout
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Tool invocations remain serialized by the existing Sequencer. Existing image preparation/copy and cleanup plus configuration writes remain the expensive awaited work. Each actual background/layout configuration change now adds one small telemetry event; image plus layout intentionally adds two sequential events.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/validate/copy an image and prune unreferenced imported images.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Bounded to the single requested image and existing imported-image cleanup for one serialized invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The agent tool already performed these filesystem operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing awaited tool work before and after the configuration change.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist one background setting and optionally one layout setting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One write for preset/removal/layout, or two sequential writes for image plus explicit layout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same writes occurred directly through IConfigurationService.updateValue.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited on the tool result path exactly as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send bounded telemetry for each actual displayed-state change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one event for a single change or two for image plus layout; duplicates are suppressed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Dispatch is not awaited; only small synchronous payload processing occurs before the configuration listener returns.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One invocation affects one pinned color scheme. An image-plus-layout request emits at most two events regardless of image size, workspace size, chat history, or imported-image count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing per-tool Sequencer serializes invocations. The two configuration writes for image plus layout remain sequential, and telemetry dispatches are asynchronous; the diff introduces no aggregate concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Resolved background state is retained per scheme and suppresses duplicate settings. Existing imported-image cleanup behavior and caches are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: tool sequencing, write order, listener behavior, and telemetry transport were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Image I/O duration varies, but it is pre-existing; the added telemetry payload has five bounded fields.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds fixed-cardinality telemetry without increasing existing file/configuration boundary counts or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Background settings change externally through settings.json, Settings UI, Settings Sync, or profile changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The configuration event synchronously checks the four relevant setting names. Only affected dark/light schemes are re-read, compared with two cached records, and logged when the shown state changed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch telemetry for externally caused displayed-background changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero to two calls per configuration event, after filtering and deduplication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: External background setting changes caused rendering/context updates but emitted no telemetry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Calls are initiated from the synchronous configuration listener, but transport completion is not awaited.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed maximum of two schemes and two emitted events for one broad configuration event; independent of the total number of settings in the profile after the event object has been built.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No explicit parallelism. At most two fire-and-forget telemetry appender calls occur for an event affecting both schemes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The two-entry reported-state map coalesces equivalent path/file-URI forms and unchanged layout/background values; it is bounded for the service lifetime.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The frequency of Settings Sync/profile events varies, but each event's added work remains fixed and filtered to four setting keys.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The listener adds constant-time checks and at most two bounded, asynchronous telemetry dispatches per relevant broad event.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and all patch pages. Traced startup/service lifetime, picker previews and commits, serialized agent-tool changes, external configuration events, configuration persistence, image filesystem work, and telemetry IPC/network dispatch. The added state is bounded to two schemes, duplicate changes are suppressed, previews do not persist or log, and new telemetry fan-out is at most two asynchronous events per logical operation; no actionable performance regression was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
